title.value: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design
title.justification: The title clearly states the focus of the paper on a method called SmOOD for detecting out-of-distribution data using surrogate neural networks specifically in the context of aircraft design.
title.quote: SmOOD: Smoothness-based Out-of-Distribution Detection Approach for Surrogate Neural Networks in Aircraft Design

extractions.description: The paper presents SmOOD, a smoothness-based out-of-distribution detection approach tailored for surrogate neural networks used in aircraft design optimization. The method aims to efficiently identify and handle out-of-distribution samples to maintain the reliability of surrogate models and thereby enhance the design process by reducing computational costs and improving prediction accuracy.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper's central theme is improving aircraft design optimization through a novel out-of-distribution detection approach, with no direct link to Climate Change or its mitigation.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Aircraft industry is constantly striving for more efficient design optimization methods in terms of human efforts, computation time, and resources consumption.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on computational methods for aircraft design rather than any specific Climate Change aspect.
primary_category.quote: Through SmOOD, our smoothness-based out-of-distribution detection approach, we propose to co-design a model-dependent OOD indicator with the optimized FNN surrogate, to produce a trustworthy surrogate model with selective but credible predictions.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary Climate Change themes or areas are addressed within the scope of this paper.
secondary_categories.quote: The paper does not touch upon any secondary themes related to Climate Change.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no relevant Climate Change sub-category that aligns with the paper's focus on aircraft design optimization using surrogate neural networks.
primary_sub_category.quote: The design of aircraft, from conceptualization to commercialization, is expensive. Their lead-time engineering process can take many years and cost billions of dollars from design to manufacture.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Similarly, there are no applicable secondary sub-categories related to Climate Change.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Various solutions have been proposed to circumvent the compute-intensive issues of MDO through surrogate modeling.

applications.value: Out-of-distribution detection in surrogate modeling for aircraft design
applications.justification: The primary application of the research is in identifying OOD samples using surrogate models for aircraft design, not directly related to Climate Change applications.
applications.quote: A trustworthy surrogate model should not only produce accurate predictions based on known context, but also detect unknown inputs and forward them to the High-Fidelity model for safe handling.

new_primary_category.quote: Aircraft industry is constantly striving for more efficient design optimization methods in terms of human efforts, computation time, and resources consumption.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is needed as the focus remains entirely on aircraft design optimization and not on Climate Change-specific issues or solutions.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Hybrid surrogate optimization maintains high results quality while providing rapid design assessments when both the surrogate model and the switch mechanism for eventually transitioning to the HF model are calibrated properly.
